ETHICS.Definition: the principles that decide which actions are right or wrong

MORALITY.Definition: the question of whether something is good or bad behaviour

WORKPLACE.Definition: the place where people do their jobs, such as an office

STRATEGIST.Definition: a person who is skilled at making plans, especially for war

PERIPHERAL.Definition: on the edge, far from the centre of power, and less important

MANUAL.Definition: a book that gives instructions and practical advice

MISSIONARY.Definition: a person sent abroad by a church to spread their religion

CREDITED.Definition: named as the reason or cause

BACKSTORY.Definition: the history and events that happened before

DISORGANISED.Definition: badly arranged; not following a clear plan

DISORDERLY.Definition: messy and without a clear structure

FORMATIONS.Definition: the arrangements in which groups of soldiers stand or move

SWEAR BY.Definition: strongly believe in the value of

DIPLOMACY.Definition: careful discussion and negotiation between countries or groups

LAST RESORT.Definition: something you do only when all other options have failed

TERRITORY.Definition: the land and area where the fighting takes place

VICTORIOUS.Definition: the winner; successful in the fight

CIRCUMSTANCES.Definition: the conditions or situations that affect what happens

BINGEING.Definition: watching a large number of, one after another

SHADOWING.Definition: a way of practising speaking by repeating audio straight after the speaker

EXPOSE.Definition: bring into contact; allow to experience

EXECUTE.Definition: carry out or put into action

INTERPRET.Definition: understand or explain in a particular way

GUIDED.Definition: helped and shown what to do
